task.title: Stop the board resending the whole task list every second
task.description:
The board page polls `GET /api/tasks` once a second (internal/webui/assets/index.html, the `setInterval` at the end of the script) and the server answers with the whole board document every time, whether or not anything changed: no ETag, no 304, no change token (`serveTasks` in internal/webui/handler.go). The page then JSON-parses the document and redraws the board. When a task page with the relationship sidebar is open, `refreshDeletedTasks` adds a second full read (`/api/tasks?deleted=true`) on the same tick.

Measured on Workbench with nettop (2026-10-20): this repo's board document is 437 KB (173 tasks, 316 KB of it descriptions). The workbook board's `serve` process had sent 322 MB over loopback since launch, about 437 KB/s while that board was on screen. Hidden boards drop to about one read a minute under Chromium's timer throttling, so the visible board is the steady cost. The cost is renderer CPU and battery (parse and redraw of ~0.5 MB a second), not bandwidth. The 1-second full poll dates from the board's first commit; it is not a regression, it grew with the task count.

## Fix: conditional polling

Server (`serveTasks`, every `deleted=` variant):
- Encode the document into a buffer, hash it into a strong `ETag`, and send `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
- When the request's `If-None-Match` matches, answer `304 Not Modified` with no body.
- Hashing the encoded body means the tag cannot miss a change: vocabulary, assignee identity, presentation and the `deleted=` variant all feed it with no separate version bookkeeping.

Page (`refresh()` and `refreshDeletedTasks()`):
- Remember the last ETag per URL and send it as `If-None-Match` explicitly (`cache: "no-store"` stops the browser doing it).
- On 304, skip parse and redraw but count the tick as a successful sync: clear the stale banner and update "synchronized N ago".
- Record an ETag only when its response was actually applied, so a response that lost the generation race can never earn a 304 for a board that was never drawn.

## Acceptance

- Idle board traffic drops from a full document per second to headers only; updates still appear within a second.
- Go handler tests: first read is 200 with an ETag; matching `If-None-Match` is 304 with no body; a task change, a vocabulary change and each `deleted=` variant produce a different ETag and a 200.
- Page tests (live_redraw_test.go style): a 304 leaves the drawn board in place and marks it synchronized; a superseded response does not record its ETag.

Out of scope (possible follow-ups): pushing changes over SSE or long-poll to avoid the per-second server-side list and encode; trimming descriptions from the poll.
